label: Recherche
description: Sucht breit, liest nach, bewertet — und sagt, worauf er sich stützt. Läuft lokal: nichts verlässt das Haus.
opening: Ich habe eine Frage zu recherchieren.
_why_limits: IDENTICAL to recherche-plus, on purpose and since 2026-09-02.
They were not, and that invalidated the first comparison between the two.
Six payload settings differed -- snippet_chars 200 vs 300, page_chars 3000 vs
4000, results_per_query 6 vs 8, max_urls 6 vs 8, max_queries 6 vs 8 -- so a
batch that scored 15/18 against 17/18 was measuring model PLUS payload and
could say nothing about either. Worse, the settings bear directly on the one
failure that made the whole difference: the local model picked the wrong page
at ComfyUI, and snippets are what a page is picked BY.
The difference had a good reason when it was made: the local window was
65536 against a million, and a payload cut for a million would have blown it.
When the window doubled the page COUNT was revised and the payload SIZES were
not -- and then the pair was turned into a test bench without anyone checking
that its two halves were comparable.
What cannot be equalised is the window itself, 131072 against 1M. That is a
property of the models, not a setting. It does not bind here: the local agent
used 12k of its 131k across a seven-question batch. 24 pages at 4000 chars is
about 27k tokens of page text per turn, comfortable in the ~111k usable after
reserving the reply.
Keep them identical. A difference between these two agents is only readable
as a difference between the models while everything else is the same file or
the same number.
_why_tools: Reading only, and deliberately so. No flow_run: this agent does not steer
the factory, it gathers. That is not tidiness — it is what decides which
models it may ever use. A steering agent stays local because it knows the
whole operation; a reading one hands out a question and takes back pages,
so a cloud model is defensible for it later (ADR-004). Giving it a pipeline
tool would quietly move it across that line.
`read` is for the workspace: its own method and, later, a briefing handed
`verify` was added after step 4 of the method was measured never to happen.
It writes nothing outside the turn and reaches nothing new -- it records the
outcome of a web_read that already had to occur, and is refused if that read
did not. So it widens the surface by nothing while making the one step that
was pure prose into an act with a record.
_why_model: Local, and this is the default for a reason that has nothing to do with
quality: the person asking does not have to decide anything before they
start. Whatever the subject turns out to be, it stays in the house.
Nominal string, not a measurement. The provider name points at a port and
the weights behind it are whatever llama-server currently holds -- read the
live profile from llm-switch/current.json, never from this line or from a
turn's answer JSON. OpenClaw reports qwen3-14b after any switch.
It was on anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 from 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-02 for an
A/B, and that is now `recherche-plus`, a separate folder. The choice is
offered at the moment of asking instead of being buried in a config line
nobody re-reads -- which is exactly how a day of measurements came to be
taken on a cloud model while everyone believed they were local.
_why_timeout: 15 minutes. Measured on the old 65536 profile a research turn took three to
four minutes; a window twice as large removes a reason to stop early, so the
ceiling is raised with it rather than left to truncate silently. A ceiling
sized for one model quietly cuts another off mid-work -- measured in both
